Full name: Igor Valeryevich Nezlobin
Date of birth: 16.05.1978
Place of birth: Murmansk
Marital status: Single
Children: None



Military specialty: Communications Engineer
Rank in RUAF: Senior Lieutenant
Callsign: Moreman


Combat experience:
After completing conscript service in the Urals, he remained in the army. In 1999, he was deployed to the Chechen Republic for combat operations. Participated in the capture of Grozny and in battles for the Shatoy district center. Awarded the Suvorov Medal and the 2nd Class Medal “For Military Valor” for his actions during the Second Chechen Campaign.

Personal profile:
Disciplined, resilient, and respectful of hierarchy. Quickly establishes trust among troops. Former comrades praise his straightforward communication and ability to boost morale of less experienced soldiers.
sample.68d3059318d70f97e704ad7f_Note_Page1_Text:
Full name: Dmitri Vladimirovich Orlov
Date of birth: 19.03.1975
Place of birth: Begezhan, Kostanay Region (since 1991, Kazakhstan)
Marital status: Divorced
Children: None



Military specialty: Platoon Commander
Rank in RUAF: Captain (retired)
Callsign: Voevoda


Combat experience:
After completing conscript service in the Vologda region, he remained in the army. In 1994, during the First Chechen Campaign, he was assigned to the Kizlyar troop group and took part in the assault on Grozny from the northern direction. During the assault, his platoon, under the command of Dmitri Vladimirovich, was encircled along with the 1st and 2nd battalions of the 131st Motor Rifle Brigade. While breaking out, all platoon members were killed or wounded, while Dmitri sustained serious injuries (noted in medical records) and was sent for treatment and rehabilitation.

In 1999, following militant incursions into Dagestan, he volunteered for the Second Chechen Campaign, personally taking part in the assault on Grozny.

For exceptional service during both Chechen campaigns, he was promoted to Captain and awarded the Order of Courage and the Medal "For Bravery" twice.


Personal profile:
Initiative-driven, responsible, but prone to acting independently. May break hierarchy if his subordinates or civilians are at risk. Conducts high-quality training of personnel. Former comrades give exclusively positive feedback, affectionately referring to Dmitri Vladimirovich as “Batya” (“Father”).
sample.68d305c35f98276b7503c336_Note_Page1_Text:
Full name: Artur Georgievich Gelovani
Date of birth: 19.08.82
Place of birth: Ordzhonikidze (renamed Vladikavkaz in 1990)
Marital status: Married
Children: None



Military specialty: Machine gunner
Rank in RUAF: Lieutenant
Callsign: Taran


Combat experience:
Served his mandatory term in special forces in the Caucasus. Due to his age, was not cleared for participation in the Second Chechen Campaign. After service, joined the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Vladikavkaz and was accepted into the FSB in 2002. Took part in the counter-terrorist operation in Beslan in 2004 and the operation to eliminate Shamil Basayev in 2006.


Personal profile:
Disciplined and resilient under stress. Though underage during the Chechen campaigns, actively participated in debris clearance and medical assistance. Completed advanced medical training prior to conscription. Married in 2001 and maintains a strong family relationship.
sample.68d305fc8c12620073059936_Note_Page1_Text:
Full name: Igor Dmitrievich Lazarev
Date of birth: 08.12.1974
Place of birth: Pushkin, Leningrad Region
Marital status: Divorced
Children: Yes



Military specialty: Sniper
Rank in RUAF: Senior Sergeant
Callsign: Strelets


Combat experience:
During his conscript service in the Leningrad Region he showed outstanding sniper skills and remained in the army, working on personnel training. He took part in the First Chechen Campaign but was wounded (noted in medical records) and after rehabilitation was assigned as a consultant to FSB units, OMON and SOBR. He did not participate in the Second Chechen Campaign, but many of Igor Dmitrievich’s trainees were awarded decorations in various conflicts.


Personal profile:
Disciplined, respects the chain of command. Among trainees and colleagues he has a reputation as a unique specialist capable of significantly increasing the effectiveness of combat teams even in field conditions.

EMP and Its Effects


An EMP (electromagnetic pulse) is used in electromagnetic weaponry (EMW).

An EMP is designed to disable electrical and electronic equipment and disrupt communication channels.

The consequences of an EMP strike include the total failure of all unshielded equipment.

After an EMP event, communication can only be maintained using analog methods and paper media.

Stay alert! Trust only verified information from official sources.
